Source: Sándor Palota, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons Hungarian President Tamas Sulyok has signed a constitutional amendment that immediately ends his term in office, formalizing a major political overhaul led by Prime Minister Peter Magyar and his ruling Tisza party. The move marks another step in Magyar’s campaign to dismantle institutions established during former Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s 16-year rule. The constitutional amendment, approved by Hungary’s parliament, cites a “serious loss of confidence” in Sulyok, who was elected president in early 2024 with support from Orban’s nationalist Fidesz party. Although Sulyok approved the legislation, he said he did so because it complied with the legal process, while warning that the measure undermines Hungary’s constitutional democracy and the rule of law. In a public statement, the former Constitutional Court judge described the amendment as a turning point for the country, arguing that removing public officials in this manner creates a dangerous precedent. He said the decision weakens democratic values, including the separation of powers and constitutional safeguards. Former Prime Minister Viktor Orban also condemned the reform, claiming it demonstrated that political power could now be used against anyone. His comments come as Fidesz continues to struggle following its decisive election defeat in April, which ended the party’s long hold on power. Under the amendment, Parliament Speaker Agnes Forsthoffer will serve as Hungary’s interim president beginning Monday until lawmakers elect a new head of state or until a new constitution comes into force. Parliament, where the Tisza party holds a two-thirds majority, has the authority to appoint a replacement. The constitutional changes also introduce a 12-year term limit for lawmakers and establish a mandatory retirement age of 70 for Constitutional Court judges. The rule will require Constitutional Court President Peter Polt, a longtime Orban ally, to step down. Since taking office, Magyar has repeatedly urged Sulyok to resign, accusing him of failing to act as a neutral head of state and instead serving the interests of Orban’s former government. Magyar said the reforms are intended to restore democratic accountability, recover public assets, and ensure the Hungarian state serves its citizens rather than entrenched political interests. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6dj.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Usmanov is described as having particularly close ties to President Putin By Robert Greenall Published 1 hour ago The European Union is to remove sanctions on two oligarchs imposed after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, according to reports, prompting anger in Ukraine. France had campaigned for Russian-Uzbek billionaire Alisher Usmanov to be taken off the list, citing "national security concerns". Luxembourg called for the removal of Russian-Israeli businessman Mikhail Fridman, who is suing the country for the release of frozen assets. Latvia initially opposed the deal but agreed to a compromise, part of which involved extending sanctions on nearly 3,000 other individuals and entities for three years. Ukrainian officials said the move was "unacceptable" and sent the wrong signal to Moscow. "Moscow is celebrating because it got what it wanted: a sense of impunity, the humiliation of the EU, and division among Europeans," Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said on X. He urged all EU member states to instead announce national sanctions on the two individuals. Latvia has already said it would do so. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov earlier welcomed the prospect of the two oligarchs being taken off the list, claiming the EU's sanctions were illegal and all Russians should be removed. Usmanov founded USM Holding company , an investment group that owns iron, steel and copper suppliers, and the Megafon telecommunications company. He has in the past had ties with the English Premier League clubs Arsenal and Everton. The EU froze his assets in 2022, describing him as "a pro-Kremlin oligarch with particularly close ties to Russian president Vladimir Putin". Usmanov said the decision was "unfair". It has been reported that France's initiative was linked to a prospective prisoner release deal with Azerbaijan. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Fridman has avoided condemning Putin outright for the war in Ukraine Fridman, a Russian-Israeli citizen born in Ukraine, is the founder of the Alfa Group investment conglomerate, with key interests in energy and banking. The EU has described him as a top Russian financier and enabler of Putin's inner circle. Fridman himself said at the time of Russia's full-scale invasion that the conflict should end as soon as possible , but avoided outright condemnation of President Putin. His Russian-Latvian business partner Pyotr Aven was stripped of Latvia's highest civilian honour in 2022 for failing to condemn the invasion of Ukraine. This may have influenced Latvia's opposition to the move, vetoing it in a vote by EU ambassadors on Monday. However, on Tuesday it changed its vote to an abstention as a compromise was reached. The new deal involved extending sanctions on some remaining 2,600 individuals and entities to three years. Until now, sanctions had to be renewed every six months. Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs also announced that France had agreed to start talks with Latvia about joining a French nuclear deterrence initiative and strengthen its military presence in Latvia. A tervek értelmében Szöul közel megháromszorozza a NATO vagyonkezelői alapjába szánt befizetéseit, így az idei 16,7 millió dollárról jövőre 50 millió dollárra emelik ezt az összeget . Dél-Korea 2024 óta fizet be az alapba – 2024 és 2025 folyamán összesen 34 millió dollárt utaltak át –, a pénzből pedig a sebesült ukrán katonák gyógykezelését, valamint katonai rehabilitációs kórházak építését finanszírozzák. A fennmaradó összegből a célzott humanitárius projektek támogatása a négyszeresére, 20 millió dollárra nő, további 30 millió dollárt pedig a fegyveres konfliktusok által sújtott országok megsegítésére szolgáló programon keresztül biztosítanak. Ezeket a forrásokat az egészségügyre, az energiaszektorra és az oktatási intézmények helyreállítására fordítják a Koreai Nemzetközi Együttműködési Ügynökségen (KOICA) és az ENSZ különböző szervezetein, köztük a világszervezet fejlesztési programján (UNDP) keresztül. A pénzügyi támogatás bővítése azért is figyelemre méltó, mert Kijev és Szöul között nemrég súlyos diplomáciai vita robbant ki. A feszültség akkor éleződött ki, amikor Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök az ENSZ Közgyűlésén bejelentette, hogy két észak-koreai hadifoglyot adnak át Dél-Koreának. Emiatt Szöul visszahívta nagykövetét és diplomáciai csapatának nagy részét Kijevből. A dél-koreai külügyminisztérium szóvivője szintén megerősítette, hogy az ország a nemzetközi közösség felelős tagjaként továbbra is kitart Ukrajna támogatása mellett.
